Customer Credit Needs Clear Limits Identify Accounts That Need Attention Establish a Consistent Credit Review Process Coordinate Sales and Accounts Teams Final Thoughts Financial Management Business Business Strategy Business Growth Product Management How Better Credit Management Can Protect Manufacturing Cash Flow | Madasky Emanproject 2 min read · Just now -- Listen Share Offering credit to customers is common in manufacturing. It helps businesses maintain commercial relationships, compete for larger orders and support regular buyers. However, when credit terms are not monitored properly, customer balances can grow faster than collections. The business continues supplying goods while an increasing amount of money remains unpaid. This can make it difficult to finance new production requirements. Customer Credit Needs Clear Limits Manufacturers should understand how much credit each customer is using and whether payments are being received within agreed terms. A customer who regularly places large orders may create significant financial exposure if the business does not review outstanding balances. Madasky recognises that customer relationships and financial discipline need to work together. Identify Accounts That Need Attention Businesses should regularly examine: Total outstanding amounts by customer. Invoices past their due dates. Customers approaching their credit limits. Repeated payment delays. Disputed invoices. Recent changes in customer payment behaviour. This allows finance and sales teams to identify concerns before they become difficult to manage. Establish a Consistent Credit Review Process Credit terms should be based on the customer’s payment history, order requirements and the manufacturer’s financial capacity. Any changes to payment conditions should be communicated clearly and approved through an appropriate process. Madasky supports businesses in strengthening management processes and improving visibility across commercial and financial activities. Coordinate Sales and Accounts Teams Sales teams need accurate information about outstanding payments before confirming additional credit-based orders. Accounts teams should also understand the commercial context of important customer relationships. When both teams work with shared information, businesses can make more balanced decisions. Final Thoughts Credit sales can support manufacturing growth, but unmanaged receivables can create unnecessary working-capital pressure. Clear credit limits, regular account reviews and timely communication help businesses protect cash flow while maintaining customer relationships. Madasky supports businesses in building stronger financial and operational discipline.
